answer: Each writer key must post a bond, and one key cannot cover another, so an attacker minting a thousand aliases locks a thousand full-price bonds. A slash burns the whole bond of the key that cheated, so each alias is a total loss, not a cheap trial. Payout is drawn per key, so added identities dilute the attacker's own yield. Each identity also solves its own cipher, paid for repeatedly. Delayed withdrawal is a time tide against mass registration. Cost outruns payout, and a pigment of good history grants no trust to the next key.
